documents.title: ICU and Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
Outside regional hospital. Admitted 02/11/2025, discharged 02/19/2025.

Presentation: Brought in overnight by his wife, who described two days of increasing sleepiness and a cough productive of green sputum, about six months after his July 2024 COPD exacerbation. On arrival he grew more somnolent and could not answer questions or give a history. Respiratory rate 28, accessory muscle use, unable to complete sentences, SpO2 88% on room air.
ABG: pH 7.28, PaCO2 60, PaO2 55, HCO3 26. Na 138, K 4.2, Cl 100, BUN 18, creatinine 1.0, WBC 15,000.
Chest x-ray: increased bronchovascular markings and a small right lower lobe infiltrate.

Diagnosis: acute-on-chronic respiratory failure due to a COPD exacerbation complicated by bacterial pneumonia (right lower lobe).

Course: Intubated in the ED for worsening somnolence with hypercapnia and admitted to the ICU. Treated with IV ceftriaxone and azithromycin, scheduled bronchodilators and systemic corticosteroids. Extubated on hospital day 3 to BiPAP, then to his home 2 L nasal cannula. Transferred to the floor day 5. Aspiration was considered as a contributor given his Zenker diverticulum; antibiotics were changed to oral clindamycin before discharge. Steroid course completed in hospital. Worked with physical therapy; walking the hall on 2 L at discharge.

Discharge medications: clindamycin 300 mg by mouth four times daily through 02/25/2025. Continue home oxygen 2 L, tiotropium, salmeterol, albuterol nebs as needed, lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25, metformin 1000 twice daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within one week; pulmonology as scheduled.

documents.title: Post-discharge phone call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called within 2 business days of discharge. Spoke with pt and wife. Home since yesterday afternoon, on 2 L, taking clindamycin four times a day. Breathing improving, cough looser. No fever. Has all meds. TCM visit confirmed for 2/25.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. ICU 2/11-2/19: COPD exacerbation with RLL pneumonia, acute-on-chronic hypercapnic resp failure, intubated 2 days. Discharge summary reviewed.
Today is his last day of clindamycin. Breathing back to his usual on 2 L, some deconditioning, short of breath on the stairs as before. Cough lighter, no fever. Eating. No diarrhea.
Wife says it scared them both; they talked again about what he would and would not want.
Exam: afebrile, sat as charted on 2 L. Coarse sounds right base improving, basal crackles. Lost about 2 kg since January.
A/P: Pneumonia/exacerbation - resolved clinically. Finishes antibiotics today. Home PT referral declined, will walk at home. Continue inhalers/O2. Weight - encouraged calories. RTC 3 months; call for any change.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Inpatient Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Inpatient GI consultation, 03/12/2025, outside regional hospital.
Asked to see a 72-year-old man with prior severe C. difficile infection, cirrhosis and chronic respiratory failure, admitted 3/10 with five days of watery diarrhea, abdominal pain and fever. He finished a course of clindamycin about two weeks ago, given after his February ICU stay for pneumonia. Stool C. difficile toxin positive on admission; started on oral vancomycin and IV metronidazole. Over the 48 hours since, the pain has worsened and he has become more tachycardic and hypotensive.
NKDA.

Vitals: T 38.7 C (101.7 F), BP 90/60, HR 110.
Exam: diffuse abdominal tenderness, rebound in both lower quadrants, hypoactive bowel sounds.
Labs today: WBC 18,000, lactate 4.5, creatinine 1.8 (baseline 1.0), BUN 35, CRP 25.
CT abdomen: colonic wall thickening without free air.

Impression: fulminant C. difficile infection, recurrence of his prior severe episode, with hypotension and rising lactate.
Recommendations: transfer to ICU; oral vancomycin 500 mg every 6 hours plus vancomycin by retention enema; continue IV metronidazole; IV fluids, vasopressor if needed; urgent general surgery consultation regarding colectomy; hold metformin, lisinopril and HCTZ while hypotensive with AKI; avoid antimotility agents. We will follow daily.
Gastroenterology

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Outside regional hospital. Admitted 03/10/2025, discharged 03/20/2025.
Diagnosis: fulminant Clostridioides difficile infection (recurrent; prior severe episode 2019), following clindamycin.
Course: Oral vancomycin and IV metronidazole from admission. Clinical worsening at 48 hours with hypotension, lactate 4.5 and AKI (creatinine 1.8) prompted ICU transfer, high-dose oral plus rectal vancomycin and surgical consultation. Brief low-dose norepinephrine for under 24 hours. General surgery followed closely; abdominal exam and lactate improved by day 4 and colectomy was not needed. Diarrhea slowed from day 6. Metronidazole stopped day 7. Creatinine 1.0 at discharge.
Home metformin, lisinopril and HCTZ held during the stay and resumed at discharge.
Discharge medications: vancomycin 125 mg by mouth four times daily for 10 days, then twice daily for 7 days, then once daily for 7 days, then every 2 to 3 days for 2 to 8 weeks per the printed schedule. Resume O2 2 L, tiotropium, salmeterol, albuterol nebs, lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25, metformin 1000 twice daily.
Allergies: NKDA. Please flag the chart: avoid clindamycin and unnecessary antibiotics.
Follow-up: PCP within one week.

conditions.label: Enterocolitis due to Clostridioides difficile, recurrent

documents.title: Post-Hospital Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, at home with Ingrid. Discharged 3/20 after fulminant C. diff - ICU, no colectomy. Diarrhea gone, one formed stool a day. Eating more. Tired. Taking vancomycin on the taper calendar the hospital gave, wife has it on the fridge. No fever, no belly pain. Breathing at baseline.
Back on lisinopril, HCTZ, metformin since discharge; home BP 110s-120s/70s.
A/P: Fulminant C. diff - clinically resolved; complete vancomycin taper. Added a chart alert to avoid unnecessary antibiotics. Labs at the May visit. Call if diarrhea returns.

documents.title: Vancomycin
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Down to the every-other-day part of the vancomycin. Pharmacy says I have 8 capsules left, is that enough to finish? Bowels normal. Fred

documents.title: RE: Vancomycin
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Fred, every other day for the remaining doses gets you to the end of the schedule with what you have. Glad the bowels are normal. Call us right away if diarrhea comes back.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Multiphase study. Treated pancreatic head mass unchanged in size. Biliary stent in place without ductal dilation. Colon now of normal wall thickness. Liver: ablation zone without enhancement; no new hepatic lesion. No ascites, no adenopathy.
reports.conclusion: Stable pancreatic head mass. No HCC recurrence. No metastatic disease.

documents.title: Oncology Follow-up
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Medical oncology 05/13/2025. Two hospitalizations this winter (pneumonia with respiratory failure; fulminant C. difficile) noted; recovered. CT 5/6 stable pancreatic head mass, no liver recurrence, no metastases. CA 19-9 70, essentially stable. AFP 5.6. Surveillance every 6 months. NKDA. Avoid clindamycin per recent C. difficile.
Medical Oncology

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u after a hard winter. Vanc taper done early May, no diarrhea since. Oncology CT stable. Breathing at baseline, using the nebulizer once a day or so.
Weight steady around 75.
Exam: sat as charted on 2 L. Crackles bases. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema.
A/P: All chronic issues at baseline. Recheck kidney function and liver tests today; will message results. RTC June for AWV.

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV. Function: independent with ADLs, slower. Ingrid manages IADLs. No falls. PHQ-2 1. AUDIT-C 0. Cognition grossly intact in conversation.
ACP revisited after the ICU stay: he was glad they intubated him and would accept it again for a short reversible illness; still no prolonged life support. MOLST completed today reflecting this; copy to wife and scanned.
Feet: monofilament intact, skin fine.
Eye exam due - optometry next month.
Vaccines: up to date except fall flu/COVID.
Labs today.

documents.title: Diabetic Eye Exam Report
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Dilated exam 7/15/2025 for diabetes. Corrected acuity 20/30 each eye. No diabetic retinopathy. Age-related lens changes, stable. Return in one year.

reports.text: High-resolution CT. Basal and subpleural reticulation with honeycombing, similar to 2023. Prior right lower lobe infiltrate has cleared. No nodule. No effusion.
reports.conclusion: Stable fibrotic lung disease. Resolved right lower lobe opacity.

documents.title: Pulmonology Follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Pulmonology 8/19/2025. ICU admission in February for hypercapnic respiratory failure with RLL pneumonia, intubated two days; recovered to baseline 2 L. HRCT 8/12: fibrosis similar, pneumonia cleared, no nodules.
Plan: continue tiotropium and salmeterol with albuterol nebs; aspiration precautions given the Zenker diverticulum; flu and COVID vaccines this fall; return in 6 months. NKDA.
Pulmonology
